c.tagline: The Valley of the Sun's resort playground of desert golf, spa retreats, Old Town nightlife and Sonoran sunsets.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but Uber and Lyft dominate; with attractions spread across the Valley, a rental car is by far the easiest way to get around, though the free Scottsdale Trolley covers Old Town.

emergency.note: 911 reaches police, fire and ambulance; summer heat is the biggest hazard, so carry water and watch for heat illness on desert trails.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Gainey Ranch: Grand Hyatt Scottsdale Resort at Gainey Ranch

avoid.reason: Old Town's bar district gets rowdy with party crowds late at night, and extreme summer heat is the bigger hazard.

hood_desc: The walkable historic core and Entertainment District, packed with galleries, boutiques, patio restaurants and the Valley's densest cluster of bars and nightclubs; the top choice for first-timers who want to be in the middle of everything.
An upscale, spread-out area of championship golf courses, luxury resorts and desert foothills beside the McDowell Sonoran Preserve; favored for golf, spa stays and quiet high-end getaways.
A master-planned residential community around man-made lakes and golf courses, with bike paths and family-friendly resorts; calm and green, roughly midway between Old Town and the northern resorts.
A polished resort-and-residential enclave built around the Hyatt Regency and a golf club, with lagoons and upscale dining at the Shops at Gainey Village; relaxed and refined.
The more affordable southern strip near the Tempe and Phoenix borders, close to the light rail, Old Town, ASU and the SkySong district, with motels, breweries and better value.

water.note: Tap water is safe though mineral-heavy; many prefer filtered for taste.

transit.pay: Valley Metro buses take cash (exact fare) or the Valley Metro app and reloadable fare passes ($2.00 a ride, $4.00 all-day); the city-run Scottsdale Trolley is free and loops Old Town, the Waterfront and nearby resorts.
transit.hours: Valley Metro buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM with limited weekend service; the free Scottsdale Trolley runs into the evening. There is no overnight transit, so rideshare fills the late-night gap.
transit.note: The Valley Metro light rail does not reach Scottsdale (it serves Phoenix, Tempe and Mesa); within the city it is buses plus the free Old Town Trolley, so most visitors rely on a rental car or rideshare to cover the sprawling metro area.

landmarks: Taliesin West
Frank Lloyd Wright's desert home and studio, a masterpiece of organic architecture built into the rugged McDowell Mountains foothills.
Old Town Scottsdale
The city's historic Western-themed district lined with adobe storefronts, galleries, and boutiques evoking classic frontier charm.
Pinnacle Peak
A jagged granite ridge with a popular switchback trail offering some of the Valley's most dramatic desert and mountain photography.
McDowell Sonoran Preserve
One of the largest urban preserves in the country, showcasing pristine Sonoran Desert landscapes, saguaros, and rugged mountain trails.
Scottsdale Museum of Contemporary Art (SMoCA)
A sleek, minimalist museum building that itself doubles as a work of contemporary architectural art in the Civic Center district.
The Wave (Scottsdale Waterfront)
A striking rippling glass-and-steel sculpture along the canal, an iconic modern landmark of the Scottsdale Waterfront district.
Soleri Bridge and Plaza
A dramatic pedestrian bridge designed by architect Paolo Soleri, its twin steel pylons cast a sundial shadow across the canal at solar noon.
Cosanti
Paolo Soleri's experimental architectural studio filled with distinctive bronze and ceramic windbells and earth-formed concrete structures.
Scottsdale Civic Center Mall
A picturesque green space with reflecting pools, art installations, and mid-century civic architecture in the heart of downtown.
Camelback Mountain (Scottsdale side)
Straddling the Phoenix-Scottsdale border, this iconic red rock landmark offers some of the region's most photographed desert skyline views.

train.note: Scottsdale has no railway station of any kind and no international or intercity trains; the Valley Metro light rail network stops short of the city, with the nearest stations in Tempe and north Phoenix. The closest Amtrak stops are Maricopa, about an hour south, on the thrice-weekly Sunset Limited between Los Angeles and New Orleans, and Flagstaff, roughly 2.5 hours north, on the daily Southwest Chief to Chicago. Amtrak Thruway buses (https://www.amtrak.com/) connect both to central Phoenix, from where a local bus or taxi is needed to reach Scottsdale. In practice almost everyone arrives by car or through Phoenix Sky Harbor airport, 20 minutes away.

bus.note: No international or long-distance coaches call at Scottsdale itself. Valley Metro (https://www.valleymetro.org/) local buses and the free Scottsdale Trolley connect to Tempe and Phoenix, where Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) run to Tucson, Los Angeles and Las Vegas from the terminal at 2115 E Buckeye Road, and Tufesa (https://tufesa.com.mx/) operates cross-border services into Sonora and beyond. Allow about 45 minutes to reach the Phoenix bus terminal from central Scottsdale, and carry a passport plus a Mexican FMM tourist card for travel past the border zone.

ferry.note: Scottsdale sits in the Sonoran Desert and has no ferries or scheduled boat services. The nearest passenger boats are sightseeing cruises on Saguaro Lake and Canyon Lake, roughly an hour east.

half.name: Sedona
half.blurb: A town among red sandstone rock formations in the Verde Valley, with hiking trails and vortex sites drawing spiritual tourism.

half.name: Apache Trail
half.blurb: A winding historic road through the Superstition Mountains past Canyon Lake and the ghost town of Tortilla Flat.

half.name: Casa Grande Ruins
half.blurb: A preserved four-story adobe structure built by the Hohokam people around 1350, sheltered under a modern roof.

half.name: Prescott
half.blurb: A former territorial capital in the pines north of Phoenix, with a historic courthouse square and Whiskey Row saloons.
